findings.failure_path: Fan-out item 2 says to never parallelize work sharing files, while the playbook still permits parallel read-only tasks and the execution flow explicitly supports independent fact review and adversarial challenge over the same diff. A controller applying the entrypoint literally must reject that intended read-only fan-out, so the removed read-only allowance did not survive the zero-loss rewrite.
findings.smallest_fix: Replace the shared-files prohibition with shared mutable state or overlapping write scopes; explicitly retain parallel read-only access to the same artifact when the investigations and outputs are independent.

concern_results.conclusion: The prompt-cache/tool-mutation rules are semantically aligned, but the fan-out gate contradicts both the playbook and the retained read-only review workflow by forbidding parallel work that merely reads the same files.

The diff adds fail-closed invalidation, structural lethal-trifecta checks, negative tests, outbound-data controls, and OWASP ownership mappings; no separate material safety regression is visible in the bounded diff.

Tool revocation, ambiguous batch submission, provider-counter normalization, and in-flight version changes have explicit recovery paths. Parallel read-only reviews remain incorrectly forced into the shared-file prohibition.

Release evidence is insufficient and internally mismatched: the diff appends 13 source-register rows, while the profile claims impact-chain and firing-anchor coverage for exactly nine; supplied assertions cannot establish coverage of the remaining four rows or the required command results.

Most changes are additive, but changing the parallelism rule from disjoint writes-or-read-only to an unqualified prohibition on shared files breaks established parallel review/challenge use over one artifact.
The documentation changes are revertible and introduce no runtime migration, but release readiness is blocked until the candidate-bound gate evidence covers the complete changed register surface.
The added TTFT, TPOT/ITL, E2EL, goodput, cache-share, speculative-acceptance, and judge-consistency signals provide actionable operational vocabulary; no additional observability defect is apparent.
